To improve policy learning, a new demonstration should begin with the explicit upward move from the start, reinforcing this as the safest initial action rather than moving LEFT. This example should carefully show foresight by steering clear of nearby fires in the central and top-edge areas, modeling how to choose and commit to the top-edge corridor path reliably. By doing so, the agent can better generalize the strategy to randomly placed fires, avoiding early mistakes and collisions with fires that were previously observed. Such a demonstration will help the agent learn a consistent, safe route in challenging and variable fire environments.
